He also condemns the police response to the demonstrations, warning that repression is unlikely to weaken a movement rooted in years of frustration over the future of public education.

items.title: Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks
items.summary: arXiv:2610.22539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The web is not static or uniform. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently. Even within a single site, successive redesigns can change how familiar features are presented and accessed. Humans adapt to this by recognizing familiar interaction patterns and reusing what they already know. We give web agents a similar ability with WebMix, a mixture hypernetwork that adapts them to unseen interfaces by composing previously trained low-rank adapters. WebMix begins with a bank of adapters trained on source interfaces.

From novels like Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn's 1966 Soviet-era Cancer Ward and Abraham Verghese's epic saga Cutting for Stone (2009) all the way through to television dramas such as Casualty, ER, and Grey's Anatomy, it seems we can’t get enough of human stories played out in a tense clinical setting. items.title: [Perspectives] Beyond the battlefield: war and global health security
items.summary: During the Syrian war (2011–24), the Assad Government forces and their Russian allies conducted hundreds of strikes on medical facilities in opposition-held areas. Monitoring groups documented over 600 attacks on health care, resulting in the deaths of hundreds of health-care workers throughout the conflict. Hospitals in eastern Aleppo and other contested regions were reduced to rubble. Surgeons operated in underground rooms illuminated by generators, and ambulances were targeted while transporting patients between sites.

items.title: [Perspectives] Temporal rationing: a man with gastric cancer in Colombia
items.summary: Pepe, a 45-year-old man living in the city of Cali, Colombia, worked as a self-employed hauler of goods with a wheelbarrow. In 2010, he presented to a general practitioner with several months of abdominal heaviness and non-exertional substernal burning. The physician provisionally diagnosed gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and prescribed omeprazole. However, Pepe's symptoms slowly worsened and 10 weeks later he returned to the physician, who ordered a gastroscopy, which occurred 2 months later, revealing an ulcerated mass.

items.title: [Editorial] Rethinking threats to human survival
items.summary: Much health advocacy is driven by single-issue activism. Communities with a common interest—from AIDS to child health, climate to tobacco control—focus intensely on their own domain. And understandably so. Important progress has been made through often courageous direct action. But this sharply competitive approach is, according to a new Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health, dangerously flawed. Indeed, perhaps the most important contribution of this Commission is to move global health beyond the consideration of individual harms.

items.summary: The theme of this year's World Mental Health Day, held on Oct 10, is Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change. On its website, WHO states that the voices of people with lived experience should “shape the policies, services and decisions that affect their lives”. While these are laudable aims, they also serve to highlight the complex challenges involved in lived experience engagement and co-production, both within the field of mental health and beyond.

items.title: [Comment] Retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes: what have we learned from TRIUMPH-2?
items.summary: It is a general observation that the degree of weight loss obtained with GLP-1 receptor agonists is less in individuals with type 2 diabetes than in people without diabetes and similar BMI. Could this difference be overcome with the new triple agonists with superior weight-lowering effects? The TRIUMPH-2 study by Virginia Bellido and colleagues1 in The Lancet is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial of the effects of retatrutide, a triple agonist (GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon), in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
